top_violation_types.title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pre-Service Training (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(2)(A))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Recited: Four out of five staff files did not have the 24-hour pre-service training available for review.

top_violation_types.title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The grassy area on one of the operations playgrounds was found to have a deep step down with the sprinkler system being exposed.

top_violation_types.title: Employee Handwashing After Removing Gloves (26 TAC §746.3415(13))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: One caregiver was observed not washing their hands after removing their gloves.

top_violation_types.title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))
Requirements for Feeding Infants - Never Prop Bottles (26 TAC §746.2419(3))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Infant was in a bouncer prop up with a bottle.

top_violation_types.title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 12 or Fewer Children (26 TAC §746.1701)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: One caregiver was observed in direct care of 11 children with three of those children being ages 0-17 months of age; the maximum number of children to be   supervised by one caregiver was 7, therefore the caregiver was over by 4 children.

top_violation_types.title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operations classrooms are out of ratio at times.

top_violation_types.title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Two infants did not have current infant feeding schedules.
